defects: Phase 1 merges the brief's stated 6-week diagnostic and 6-week design stages into one 12-week 'Design' phase, cutting the diagnostic to four weeks (W1, W2) and dropping a diagnostic sign-off, contrary to the five stages the client stated.

W6 runs the routine in the pilot districts for only four weeks (17-20), so D9 judges pilot-district losses against the pre-pilot baseline on two to three weeks of data, too little to test the first success criterion.
W8 trains crews only in the first rollout districts and W9 only coaches crews as districts go live, so no stream trains crews in the later districts that the all-districts criterion depends on.
W4 (weeks 9-12), W7 (weeks 18-20) and W10 (weeks 26-33) are marked 'after' W3, W6 and W9 yet start before those streams end.
W5 confirms pre-pilot loss levels in the pilot districts but produces no deliverable, so Workshop 3 and the week 20 gate have no signed-off pre-pilot baseline for the first success criterion.
W6 runs the routine in the pilot districts for only three weeks (18-20) after five weeks of readiness in W5, so D8 tests the first success criterion on one to two weeks of loss data.
The diagnostic streams W1 and W2 both quantify and locate losses by district and neither examines how crews find and fix leaks today, although W3 must design a new leak-detection routine.
W4 pilot plan starts in week 9, before the week 10 check-in confirms the program and routine design as its basis, and is marked 'after W3' while W3 runs to week 10.
W7 (weeks 19-20), W9 (weeks 24-33) and W12 (weeks 37-39) are marked 'after' W6, W8 and W11 yet start before those streams end.
W8 is to 'train district crews before each wave' but ends in week 25 while W10 launches waves through week 33, so later waves have no training slot.

why: Y keeps the client's five stated stages with their exact lengths and a gate closing each, and adds a pre-pilot baseline deliverable (D5) and an explicit out-of-scope guard, so its defects can be fixed inside a correct skeleton. X has the stronger diagnostic and a slightly longer pilot run, but it overrides the brief's stage structure and shortens the diagnostic, which is the harder defect to justify to the client.
